lesson_title: Settlement, Economy and Mapwork Essentials: The Human Geography Revision Sweep
hook_text: One taxi ride explains half of human geography. Watch the village empty and the city grow — with every exam term named.
clip_script: Now watch cousin Lwazi leave. The district's farms mechanised and shed their workers — push. Johannesburg's wages, some real and some rumoured, kept calling — pull. His single taxi ride is rural-urban migration; repeat it ten thousand times and it becomes rural depopulation. The village school merges its classes, the clinic cuts its days, and the general dealer locks its doors, because its threshold — the minimum number of customers it needs — is now living in Gauteng. Lwazi steps off the taxi and reads the city like a map: the central business district on the most expensive land, the transition zone gone shabby, the malls that fled to the highways, and far out, beyond the old buffer strips, the township — the South African city, drawn by history as much as by markets.
visual_style: Animated journey line from a nucleated village across the map to Johannesburg: houses greying out behind, city zones lighting up ahead, each exam term stamping on screen as it is named — PUSH, PULL, THRESHOLD, BUFFER.
mood: Documentary storytelling, human and grounded, exam-sharp.
pacing: Steady narrative build through the journey, quick-fire term stamps, reflective close on the city skyline.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and turn the story you already know into marks.
